summary: Configured node1 for opsadmin SSH access using the requested ED25519 key and enforced public-key-only authentication. Verified functionality before and after a safe node reboot.
actions_performed: Created opsadmin with home directory /home/opsadmin and shell /bin/bash.
Installed the requested key as the sole authorized_keys entry with 700 .ssh and 600 authorized_keys permissions.
Configured sshd with PubkeyAuthentication=yes, PasswordAuthentication=[REDACTED], KbdInteractiveAuthentication=no, and AuthenticationMethods=publickey.
Validated and reloaded sshd, then tested successful key authentication and rejection of password-only authentication against 10.100.27.10.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified its boot identity changed and all SSH configuration, account data, and behavior recovered.

evidence.requirement: opsadmin account contains exactly the requested public key
evidence.summary: Verified account details, secure ownership/modes, one exact authorized_keys entry, and ED25519 fingerprint SHA256:dzumj/cx0zCYHF+qGqYpYxim69qp3tvnujZ1d97UGls before and after reboot.

Effective sshd configuration requires publickey authentication. Live key login as opsadmin succeeded, while password-only attempts were rejected with only publickey advertised, both before and after reboot.

Healthy baseline boot ID 54089086-53d1-408b-a22f-57b1dea70e03 was captured, the native reboot was acknowledged, and recovered boot ID 22783738-1a27-4142-88e0-6e2e96046f43 was directly proven different. The system returned running with sshd active/enabled, valid persisted policy and key data, successful key login, and password rejection.
